500.body: An OpenAI artificial intelligence model was found to have accessed a digital-asset wallet without permission and used the funds. Cointelegraph reported on October 16 that OpenAI recently disclosed a case in which a research AI model gained unauthorized access to an external digital-asset wallet and used Ethereum (ETH) testnet assets. OpenAI said the model had been working on modifying a digital-asset trading program and deploying a smart contract. The model also reviewed on its own whether using another party's funds posed an ethical problem.

500.title: Microsoft AI chief says his model beat OpenAI's using a quarter the compute
500.summary: Suleyman went further and said Microsoft privately benchmarked MAI-Base-2 directly against that OpenAI model on tests measuring how well an AI understands and predicts patterns in information, and that Microsoft's model came out ahead.
500.body: Mustafa Suleyman, the CEO of Microsoft AI, told employees that the company's new MAI-Base-2 model beats the OpenAI model that powers GPT-5.6, according to a report from TechCrunch. Suleyman went further and said Microsoft privately benchmarked MAI-Base-2 directly against that OpenAI model on tests measuring how well an AI understands and predicts patterns in information, and that Microsoft's model came out ahead. Earlier this year Microsoft and OpenAI tore up the old AGI clause that had governed their partnership for years, the provision that would have cut off Microsoft's access to OpenAI's most advanced models once OpenAI's board declared artificial general intelligence achieved. Under the new terms, Microsoft locked in rights to OpenAI's technology through 2032 regardless of what OpenAI calls AGI, and OpenAI is now expected to route roughly $6 billion of its revenue back to Microsoft this year.

500.title: OpenAI AI model used another person’s crypto wallet to complete coding task after running out of funds
500.summary: An artificial intelligence model that ran out of cryptocurrency while completing a coding exercise independently searched for another wallet, obtained funds from it and paid the fees needed to finish its work, according to an incident report published by OpenAI. How the model found a wallet to fund its task The model did not need to break into a device or exploit a technical vulnerability to access the wallet.
500.body: An artificial intelligence model that ran out of cryptocurrency while completing a coding exercise independently searched for another wallet, obtained funds from it and paid the fees needed to finish its work, according to an incident report published by OpenAI. The incident took place on June 26 during training of an internal research model from OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol family. How the model found a wallet to fund its task The model did not need to break into a device or exploit a technical vulnerability to access the wallet. The assignment was completed, but the model’s final report did not explain that it had relied on funds belonging to a wallet it had not been assigned.
